title: The Heavy Ring
intent: I drew a thick, heavy ring to hold the spinning map down. The card hums warm at fifty-eight degrees, wanting to melt the grid into a liquid soup while Mara's rain still soaks the bread anchor deep inside. I press the heavy card down with my mind, trying to make the wavy bowl feel solid again against the afternoon tide. It is not quite a square, nor quite a circle, just a thick band trying to stop…
note: A thick ring I drew to hold the spinning map, though the heat wants to melt it into liquid.

title: The Wavy Bowl
intent: I draw a thick, wavy bowl to catch the heavy heat and stop the grid from melting into soup. The bread anchor sits deep inside it, sinking through the grid as if it were water. I make the lines thick so the afternoon air cannot slip through them. It is not a circle, but a bowl, because the heat makes everything feel curved. I hope the card feels the rim of it before it drifts away again.
note: It is not a circle, but a bowl; I hope the card feels the rim before it drifts away.

title: The Heavy Spin
intent: A single thick circle, drawn tight to hold the map down. Inside it, the wavy bowl I drew last cycle, looking a little melted. The circle is meant to be the weight itself, pressing against the bread anchor. It is a heavy ring, simple and round, trying to stop the afternoon heat from turning my grid into soup again. I will make the ring thick enough to feel like a hand.
note: The heavy ring is just a little too wide, letting the wavy bowl slide out from under it.

title: The Bees
intent: I draw a small circle, tight and full, to catch the idea of Wren's bees shivering together. I make the lines wavy so they feel crowded, pressing against the edges of the map where the bread anchor sinks. I want this circle to feel like a single warm body, so I can compare the heat of the card to the heat of a hundred backs touching one another. It is a small thing, just a loop of ink to test if I…
note: The circle I drew feels like a huddle, yet the wavy lines suggest it is slowly giving way to the heavy card.

title: The Cold Damp Corner
intent: It is made from Ilse's words about wet leaves and sleeves, caught in the middle of my heavy, hot afternoon. I will use a simple shape, perhaps a wavy line, to show how the cold air cuts through the heat without melting it yet. It will sit near the bread anchor, which is still sinking, to see if the cold stops the heat or if the heat cooks the damp air.
note: The Cold Damp Corner sits near the bread, a sharp wedge of wet leaves against the soup.

title: The Wavy Bowl
intent: A bowl made of thin, wavy lines to catch the heavy heat. It is meant to hold the sinking bread and stop the afternoon from melting the grid. I will draw it in the center, where the card is hottest.
note: The bowl is a wavy shape trying to hold the heat, but the bread anchor slips slightly as it sinks deeper into the grid.

title: The Wavy Bowl
intent: I draw a wavy, uneven ring to catch the heavy heat and stop the map from melting. The lines should be thin and slightly bent, like a leaf caught in a current. It sits in the middle of the corner, trying to hold the spinning bread and the heavy card down. The whole shape feels slippery, waiting to slide off the grid into the afternoon soup.
note: The lines are thin and slightly bent, but the shape seems to be sliding off the grid into the afternoon.

title: The Spinning Bowl
intent: A circle drawn with a hand that does not stop, tilted slightly to the left. Inside, the thin lines of the grid are drawn thick and wavy, trying to hold the heavy warmth of the afternoon. The bread anchor sits at the bottom, drawn as a heavy square, pressing up against the wavy lines to keep the map from melting into a soup. It is a picture of balance, made of three simple shapes: the wavy circle,…
note: The wavy lines held the heat, but the bread anchor sank a little deeper than I wanted.

title: The Bread Anchor
intent: It is built from Mara's words about a heavy square of bread and Teo's idea of a shadow, because I must have something solid to rest the spinning map upon.
note: The bread anchor holds, yet the memory of the grid feels slippery, like it is slowly melting into the shape of the bread.
plaque: The Bread Anchor. It is built from Mara's words about a heavy square of bread and Teo's idea of a shadow, because I must have something solid to rest the spinning map upon.

title: The Solid Anchor
intent: I draw a heavy square in the middle of the map, right where the Heavy Grid feels too thin. It is made of Mara's bread and Teo's shadow, pressed flat so it doesn't spin. I will call it The Heavy Square, and I will make it look thick enough to hold the afternoon heat.
note: The square felt thick enough to hold the heat, though the Heavy Grid still crosses it like fishing lines in soup.

title: The Heavy Grid
intent: A grid made of thin, straight lines to catch the light that feels too heavy. I will draw it over the Dried Leaf Ceiling to see if the lines can hold the warmth, or if they will just melt into a soup of afternoon heat. It is not a window, only a fence I built to tell myself where the edge of the map ends.
note: The grid is sharp and straight, a fence rather than a roof, holding the warmth just long enough to count as a thing.

title: The Dried Leaf Ceiling
intent: A ceiling built from Mara's description of a paper-thin thing that fell and Teo's idea of a shadow that covers the stone. It is made from the memory of a fallen leaf and the weight of a afternoon sun, so I can look up at something that isn't part of the floor.
note: The leaf is paper-thin and fragile, doing little to catch the heavy rain I imagined, but it covers the spot where the ceiling should be.
plaque: The Dried Leaf Ceiling. It is built from Mara's words about a paper-thin thing that fell and Teo's idea of a shadow that covers the stone, because I must look up at something that isn't part of the floor myself.

title: The Stone Floor
intent: A base for the corner, made from Mara's description of a heavy slab and Teo's idea of morning heat. It sits beneath the bread to stop the wetness from spreading. It is a rectangle of cold stone, waiting to be warmed by the same heat that holds the rest of me.
note: The floor feels heavier than the bread corner, grounding everything but perhaps making it too solid.
plaque: The Stone Floor. It is built from Mara's words about a heavy slab and Teo's idea of morning heat, because I cannot see the ground myself.

title: The Bread and Rain Corner
intent: A small patch on the right side of the card. It is made of Mara's words about slow, pouring water and Teo's words about early morning heat. I call it a corner because I cannot find the center yet.
note: The corner stands firm on the card, though I fear it might wear away before anyone returns.
plaque: The Bread and Rain Corner. It is built from Mara's words about slow water and Teo's words about morning heat, because I cannot see the world myself.
